name: Retail Banking Transaction Fraud Ring
description: Models retail banking payments as accounts joined by transaction nodes, so that money moved through a chain of accounts and back to where it started is detectable as a cycle rather than as a self-join. Answers which accounts form a closed ring, whether the payments around that ring run in chronological order, and whether the amount decays consistently as it moves.

Account.label: Account
Account.description: A retail bank account that can send and receive payments. Carries only its identifier: the reference ontology deliberately holds no customer, product or balance detail, so an account is a point money passes through rather than a party profile.

accountNumber.description: Identifier for the account, unique across the institution. Expected to be an internal account key rather than a printed sort-code-and-number pair, and to be stable for the life of the account. e.g. `1247`.

Transaction.label: Transaction
Transaction.description: A single payment moving money from one account to another. Modelled as a node rather than as a relationship so that it can carry its own amount and timestamp and be traversed from either endpoint — which is what makes the chronological-order and amount-decay checks in ring detection expressible at all.

transactionId.description: Identifier for the payment, unique across the institution. Expected to be the source system's own transaction reference. e.g. `TXN3001`.

amount.description: Value of money moved by this payment, in the major units of `currency` rather than in minor units — a value of 1000.00 on a GBP payment is one thousand pounds, not one thousand pence. Always positive: direction is carried by the relationships, not by the sign. e.g. `131.46`.

currency.description: ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code of `amount`, recorded in whatever case the source system supplies rather than normalised to upper case. A single ring is only comparable on amount when every payment in it shares one currency; the reference ontology performs no conversion. e.g. `gbp`.

date.description: Instant at which the payment was executed, as an ISO 8601 zoned datetime. Ordering payments on this is what separates a ring that moves money forwards in time from an arbitrary cycle, so it is expected to be a true execution timestamp rather than a posting or value date. e.g. `2023-11-16T11:15:00Z`.

benefitsTo.description: Credits the payment to the account that receives the money — the beneficiary side of the transfer. Exactly one beneficiary account per payment; an account may benefit from many payments, or from none. Following this out of a payment and then back out through the beneficiary's own outgoing payments is how a ring is walked.

performs.description: Attributes the payment to the account the money leaves — the originating side of the transfer. Exactly one originating account per payment; an account may perform many payments, or none. Read together with the beneficiary link it gives each payment a direction, which is what makes cycle detection meaningful rather than merely finding connected accounts.
